rules.response: Conditionals let your program make decisions. 'if' checks a condition; 'elif' checks another condition if the first was False; 'else' runs when no condition matched. Every if/elif/else line must end with a colon (:). The code inside must be indented with 4 spaces.

An IndentationError means your code inside an if/elif/else/for/while/def block is not properly indented. Python requires exactly 4 spaces (or 1 tab, consistently) for code inside a block. Make sure all lines inside the block are aligned.

A SyntaxError before running often means a missing colon (:) at the end of an if, elif, else, for, while, or def line. Check that every such line ends with a colon. Also look for mismatched brackets or missing quotes.

You can place an if statement inside another if statement — this is called nesting. Each nested level needs an additional 4 spaces of indentation. Be careful not to nest too deeply, as it makes code harder to read.
